key_insight: A PBRL framework that infers per-annotator reliability and adaptively trusts, ignores, or flips their pairwise preferences, producing robust reward models and policies even with noisy or adversarial annotators.
problem_solved: How to learn reliable reward signals and policies from preference data collected from heterogeneous annotators (accurate, noisy, or adversarial) where treating all feedback equally or naively filtering fails.
method: Estimate annotator reliability from aggregated pairwise comparisons and classify feedback as Trust / Don't Trust / Flip.
Reweight or correct (flip) adversarial/noisy preferences to produce a denoised preference dataset.
Train a reward model on corrected preferences and use it with standard RL to learn robust policies.
impact: Enables practical deployment of preference-based RL with mixed-quality human feedback by improving robustness to malicious or low-quality annotators, reducing manual curation and improving policy reliability.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: multi-expert pairwise comparisons → annotator reliability inference → trust/don't-trust/flip decisions → reward model → RL agent

paper_title: Trust, Don't Trust, or Flip: Robust Preference-Based Reinforcement Learning with Multi-Expert Feedback
paper_authors: Seyed Amir Hosseini, Maryam Abdolali, Amirhosein Tavakkoli, Fardin Ayar, Ehsan Javanmardi
